concept.title: What Is a Passphrase?
concept.shortdesc: A passphrase is a series of words used to protect an account. A long, unique passphrase can be easier to remember and harder to guess than a short password.

section.title: Understand passphrases
section.p: A passphrase is a password made up of a sequence of words. Its length helps make it difficult for cybercriminals to guess or crack, while the words can make it easier for you to remember.

NC State recommends using passphrases instead of relying only on short passwords with a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. A passphrase should be long and difficult for someone else to guess.

section.title: Use a different passphrase for every account
section.p: Create a unique passphrase for each account. Do not reuse the same passphrase, or a slightly changed version of it, across your NC State and personal accounts.

If a cybercriminal obtains a passphrase used for one account, reusing it could put other accounts at risk. Those accounts may contain personal information, university information, financial records, or other sensitive data.

section.title: Manage passphrases securely
section.p: Remembering a different passphrase for every account can be difficult. A password manager can securely store login credentials and may generate strong passwords for you. You generally need to remember only the password that protects the password manager.

NC State's source article identifies LastPass Enterprise as available to NC State employees. Availability for students, visitors, or other account holders is not established by that article. Check current NC State licensing and guidance before choosing an institution-provided password manager.

section.title: Add another layer of account protection
section.p: Use two-factor authentication (2FA) when an account offers it. NC State uses Duo Security for 2FA on applicable university accounts. Two-factor authentication adds a verification step beyond your passphrase.

section.title: Follow NC State password guidance
section.p: For requirements that apply to NC State accounts, consult the NC State Password Guidelines and the Password Standard.
If you need assistance, contact the NC State IT Service Portal or call 919-515-4357 (HELP).
section.note: Do not use a passphrase example published in an article or training material as your own passphrase. Create a new, unique passphrase that is not publicly known.
